title.narrative: Sierra Leone inter-faith action towards credible, free, fair and non-violent election

description.narrative: This project aims to contribute to ensuring there is a peaceful, free, fair credible and non- violence elections process in 2018 Elections. The announcement of elections in 2018 came at the backdrop of a number of socio-economic and political challenges the country has been grappling with. This includes the outbreak of the Ebola virus and the collapse of the mining sector that exposed the fragility of the country’s economic growth pattern resulting in loss of jobs and revenue for the country. Ebola in particular was as much a health crisis, as a crisis of governance. It exposed the country’s weak health system and brought to the fore the demand for increased accountability of national resources following the Ebola audit that highlighted mismanagement and misappropriation of funds. With women and young people particularly affected by the Ebola outbreak and a weak opposition mired in violence and serious internal wrangling to hold the government to account, the 2018 elections raise the spectre of political disaffection, disillusionment and isolated violence in a bitter struggle – both at party and national level – to succeed the outgoing President.The project rationale is further basing on the role and experiences of faith leaders in the recent Ebola outbreak, where faith leaders exhibit their local legitimacy beyond just mediation and reconciliation. Therefore, this approach is seeking to utilise an independent but also much broad based system to the 2018 election cycle in promoting civic education, peace messages and in supporting the efforts of the EMB and other actors targeting vulnerable groups including women, people with disability, young people (first time voters for example) in the electoral process.
